# 14 SEO

## Static SEO files

* `robots.txt` allows all crawlers and declares `https://zombiebases.com/sitemap.xml`.
* `sitemap.xml` is generated by `scripts/generate-sitemap.py`.
* `google4e6ab63a51472490.html` is a Google verification file.
* `CNAME` sets the custom domain.

## Client SEO helper

`js/seo.js` exposes `window.seo`, including production origin, default image, description truncation, metadata setters, canonical handling and JSON-LD insertion/removal.

## Page metadata patterns

* Homepage applies WebSite/SearchAction and ItemList structured data.
* Base detail applies article/place-like structured data and canonical clean URL metadata.
* Rankings and scenarios apply ItemList structured data.
* Compare applies comparison-specific titles/descriptions.
* Field Manual applies long-form page metadata.

## Canonical URL assumptions

The production origin is hard-coded as `https://zombiebases.com`. Base pages prefer clean canonical URLs. Query-driven filters generally avoid treating each filter state as a separate canonical content page.

## Sitemap contents

The sitemap generator includes key static pages and base routes. It includes both clean base URLs and legacy `base.html?slug=` URLs, which preserves discovery but may duplicate canonical targets unless canonical tags are respected.

## Structured data caveat

Structured data is inserted client-side. Crawlers that do not execute JavaScript may not see page-specific JSON-LD or updated title/canonical tags for dynamic shells.

## SEO risks

* Base detail HTML source is generic until JavaScript runs.
* Query and clean routes can represent the same content.
* Region/type/scenario pages are query-driven rather than clean canonical route families.
* Duplicate sitemap entries for legacy and clean routes need canonical discipline.
* Fictional survival analysis should avoid being marked up as real emergency guidance; V1 uses general website/item/article/place-like data rather than emergency schemas.
